scope: Commit-29 conversion-guide claims against the parser and consumers

claims: a value of zero disables sharding

preexisting_implementation.allocator: compile.py multiplies shard_size by 1024**2 and starts a new shard whenever current_shard_size + size exceeds that limit and the current shard is nonempty; no zero-disables branch exists.

shard_size_documentation.scalar_transcription: A standard-library transcription rejected 1.5 with argparse exit code 2 and allocated three shards for positive module sizes [100, 200, 300] at a zero-byte threshold.
shard_size_documentation.reach: The parent-tree search found conversion main as the sole direct compile_model caller.
shard_size_documentation.limits: Repository conversion, safetensors serialization and filesystem writes were not executed.

resume_documentation_observation.documentation: The guide says saved arguments are restored on resume and that some may be overridden.
resume_documentation_observation.source_behavior: Non-None parser defaults overwrite stored checkpoint_interval, devices and device_ratios values when those options are omitted. Devices emits a warning when changed; the empty device_ratios default does not.
resume_documentation_observation.example_reach: After the guide's multi-GPU command, its resume-only command continues on device 0 with no ratios rather than restoring the saved device list and ratios.
resume_documentation_observation.status: confirmed_source_observation; combined ledger candidate not yet created

other_documentation_observations: The declared resume option is -resume/--resume; argparse accepts documented -r as an unambiguous prefix.
The documented head_bits range 1 through 8 has no parser or prepare range check.
An existing output directory is not cleared; same-named files may be replaced while unrelated files remain.
checkpoint_interval is a minimum interval checked after modules, not an exact interval.
The claim that extra devices use very little memory is unsupported at low bitrates by the per-device scratch-buffer arithmetic and was not measured.
limits: No conversion, GPU workload or filesystem-writing operation was executed.
Argparse and shard-allocation checks were transcriptions of inspected source.
Performance and memory-use claims were not benchmarked.
